full_chain_observation.finding: Client setup registers factories once through the shown setup callback. The BUTTON factory constructs both the live widget and its corresponding configuration screen; concrete dispatch is by registered widget type.
Right click requires hovered widget in programming area, obtains model from widgetMap, requests configuration screen, captures configuringMCWidget and switches to that screen only if nonnull.

Config screen owns translatable title; init computes guiLeft/guiTop from its own width/height. Text/tooltip fields and enable condition are populated from retained model; parent editor is return/update destination.
Button settings add their own width/height and click-assignment fields. Labels use translated captions and measured width to align the two size fields, while numeric X/Y/Z markers remain literal.

Player-global/server-global prefix controls change list contents and displayed prefix. Enable variable namespace and click variable namespace are separate fields of this same editor flow, not separate reference instances.

onClose creates replacement model from current fields, sends it to editor when nonnull, then sets editor current. Text parsing accepts component JSON or wraps plain text; parse error becomes literal error component rather than blocking close.

Edited widget record preserves position via existing WidgetSettings, changes text/size through new records, and carries enable variable and value separately from click variable/value. This is model ownership distinct from a live AbstractWidget identity.

Editor update applies only when configuringMCWidget nonnull, still mapped, and current model unequal to replacement. It replaces model at old widget key, clears configuringMCWidget and requests rebuild. Equal/missing path does not clear it in this method.

Rebuild branch copies retained model values into a new LinkedHashMap of newly constructed controls, adds renderables, then clears old map and replaces it. Import/pastebin/empty branches precede this branch and remain distinct source conditions; no claim all entry paths necessarily enter rebuild branch.

Programming/tray coordinates are evaluated relative to current getGuiLeft/getGuiTop. Drag stores replacement model coordinates relative to editor origin, not absolute screen coordinates. Drag/copy variants belong to same editor and receive zero separate credit.

Editor close selects only widgets whose current widget position lies in programming area, then requests item save and update packet if current hand holds remote item. UI close request is observed; full server persistence/application was not reviewed.

Live remote init obtains saved layout, creates controls with this screen owner and computes each visible flag from enable predicate. Editor requests same builder without filtering. This source uses visible, not active, for enable condition.

Empty enable variable permits visible state; otherwise read player-context position with ZERO default and compare whole BlockPos to enablingValue. Percent variables select server-global store via helper; hash/unprefixed variables select player store.

Packet handler invokes helper setPos/setStack before, on clientbound flow, calling current-screen refresh dispatcher. Dispatcher acts only if current Minecraft.screen is RemoteScreen, not retained editor/config screens.

For changed variable name matching a variable widget, invoke its factory-specific callback. Regardless of that match, every mapped widget message is reparsed and visible recomputed from enable condition. BUTTON factory inherits empty per-variable callback, yet generic visibility refresh still runs.

Live button geometry is local model coordinates plus current screen origin. Click callback sends position packet only when click var name nonempty. Tooltip is retained model component; drawing/click/state ownership is explicit but network success not proven.

RemoteScreen.init as read adds newly built controls to retained widgetMap without explicit clear in these classes. Generic base selected init does not prove all lifecycle cleanup or absence of stale references. Do not treat this source as a proven flawless resize implementation.
